### 4. AI Changes The Finance Landscape

McKinsey estimates that AI-powered improvements in productivity could add [an extra $340 billion of value per year to the banking sector](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/mckinsey-digital/our-insights/the-economic-potential-of-generative-ai-the-next-productivity-frontier#key-insights), if all use cases were implemented.

And research from Citi found that AI could [increase the industry’s profits by 9%](https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2024/citi-publishes-new-report-ai-in-finance) in the next four years, taking them close to the $2 trillion mark.

**_![Image 17: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/wEbVmzDaSbuCRB6cmCcJ)Searches for “AI in finance” are up 809% in 5 years._**

**Autonomous finance includes everything from customer service chatbots to automated forecasting to AI-powered fraud detection.**

**_![Image 18: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/ZDvZYKyEQbSfdlhtCoCQ)With AI, tasks like fraud monitoring, customer support, and personalized marketing[can be automated](https://www.businessinsider.com/chatgpt-and-generative-ai-in-financial-services-hype-next-prepare-2023-may)._**

[50% of finance CFOs](https://www.syntellis.com/resources/report/2024-cfo-outlook-financial-institutions) plan to implement AI within customer experience tools in the next 12 to 18 months.

And almost 1 in 4 (24%) are already using AI when it comes to fraud prevention, with a further 36% planning to introduce it.

Data from NVIDIA shows most [AI interest in the financial sector](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/industries/finance/ai-financial-services-report/) is focused on data analytics.

**_![Image 19: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/m1U7ytYMRy2kHLIXsmN9)Almost 7 in 10 financial services professionals say their company has adopted AI for data analytics._**

Advanced analytics ties into fraud prevention, with AI able to comb datasets for sophisticated fraud patterns.

There’s also a risk management element, with anomalies in investments and loans able to be identified more easily.

For example, [Zest AI](https://www.zest.ai/) offers an AI platform focused on lending.

Their AI helps banks spot good borrowers and avoid those who are likely to default.

It can actually challenge human bias: Zest has helped lenders increase approvals for [Latinos by 49%](https://www.zest.ai/insights/zest-ais-credit-models-proven-to-increase-loan-approvals-for-every-protected-class)and Black applicants by 41% while keeping risk constant.

And its customer base has grown by 50% annually since 2020.

One credit union with assets of $2.2 billion automated [between 70 and 83% of all its consumer loan decisions](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6179287a90a6ea0e76461eba/666b6814839d3d38b1600e00_Commonwealth%20Credit%20Union%20Case%20Study.pdf) after implementing Zest’s platform.

**_![Image 20: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/QJXGCCnhSUurCFNkwYBK)AI-powered lending benefits banks and borrowers._**

[Portrait Analytics](https://portrait-analytics.com/) is another company looking to drive bottom-line results in the finance industry.

The startup’s offering is an AI investment analyst.

It’s a natural language processing platform that’s based on generative AI.

Analysts usually spend hours reading and analyzing company filings, but this AI application extracts that data and automatically summarizes the key information.

It’s [as much as 10x faster than human analysts](https://www.unusual.vc/post/portrait-analytics-seed), which allows firms to save time and realize new investment opportunities before the competition.

The company raised $7m in seed funding last year.

### 5. Healthcare Further Embraces AI

Goldman Sachs reports that [more than 25% of the work done by healthcare professionals](https://www.dropbox.com/s/1u7fz3d9sglzxrl/Global-Economics-Analyst_-The-Potentially-Large-Effects-of-Artificial-Intelligence-on-Economic-Growth-Briggs_Kodnani.pdf) in the United States could currently be automated by AI.

**_![Image 21: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/aUPWVU1lQHG3L18jnTH8)Goldman Sachs estimates that 28% of work done by healthcare practitioners could be automated by AI._**

Researchers from McKinsey and Harvard estimate that AI-enabled cost savings could top [$360 billion per year](https://www.nber.org/papers/w30857) within the next five years.

There’s already a history of AI being used for things like radiology, pathology, and patient monitoring.

It was [even used as part of the development of COVID-19 vaccines](https://www.pfizer.com/news/articles/how_a_novel_incubation_sandbox_helped_speed_up_data_analysis_in_pfizer_s_covid_19_vaccine_trial#:~:text=mRNA%20and%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20for%20Advanced%20Vaccine%20Innovation&text=As%20Pfizer%20scientists%20raced%20to,to%20help%20achieve%20this%20mission.).

In total, [more than 650 AI-enabled devices](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/13/3/498#:~:text=The%20FDA%20has%20approved%20AI,to%20the%20radiology%20medical%20subspecialty.)have already been approved by the FDA. These are AI applications that directly impact patient care.

**_![Image 22: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/pQqSGPcURFyAW1zl2es6)The vast majority of current AI applications are in radiology._**

The first algorithm was approved in 1995, but there wasn’t much development until 2019. Between that year and 2023, there were more than 400 algorithms approved.

And new AI developments are surging.

**[Precision medicine](https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbestechcouncil/2023/01/24/ais-biggest-promise-the-democratization-of-precision-medicine/?sh=794d28a61ba1) is one potential application of [AI in healthcare](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/healthcare-ai).**

This refers to each patient being treated based on individual, unique parts of their DNA, medical history, imaging, and so on.

AI platforms will be able to analyze all of the patient’s data and recommend a tailored course of treatment specifically for that patient.

Today, this exists in the form of treating patients based on specific gene expressions, like certain cancers.

However, experts say the AI technology will soon encompass more data points and be [applicable to diseases like Alzheimer’s](https://karger.com/mpp/article/doi/10.1159/000538251/897933/Alzheimer-s-Disease-A-Suitable-Case-for-Treatment), obesity, and depressive disorders.

**_![Image 23: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/nbyDw9zQxms41Qf07R3Q)Searches for “precision medicine” have grown by 26% in the last 5 years._**

In one current example, [Avenda Health](https://avendahealth.com/) has launched an AI platform for managing and treating prostate cancer.

The solution combines patient data, imaging, biopsies, and pathology into a deep-learning algorithm. It then determines the extent of the cancer and creates a 3D cancer estimation map along with optimal treatment possibilities.

In clinical trials, the use of the platform resulted in treatment changes [28% of the time](https://mobile.hospimedica.com/artificial-intelligence/articles/294797002/ai-platform-analyzes-data-from-prostate-imaging-biopsies-and-pathology-to-identify-tumor-location.html). Most often, these changes resulted in more localized treatment of the cancer.

Avenda claims that [its AI can identify 159% more cancer than MRI alone](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/avenda-health-deploys-ai-cancer-imaging-technology-at-kasraeian-urology-improving-local-access-to-cutting-edge-prostate-cancer-care-302150527.html).

**_![Image 24: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/XT08WSgT2QBEwyGS9OIw)Avenda’s Unfold AI system improves location mapping and treatment of prostate cancer._**

Some in healthcare believe that AI may even go as far as [replacing physicians](https://www.economist.com/leaders/2024/03/27/the-ai-doctor-will-see-youeventually) in many aspects of the job.

Researchers from [The Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University](https://insight.kellogg.northwestern.edu/article/will-ai-replace-doctors) say this transformation may be as little as a few decades away. But, they caution, there will still be a need for empathy, compassion, and human interaction from doctors.

**Another future application of AI in healthcare is in pharmaceutical development.**

**_![Image 25: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/2gczZ7jSaOsC7FVsYsWv)Search volume for “AI drug discovery” is up 929% in the past 5 years._**

The total expense involved in bringing a drug to final approval is [estimated at an average of $1 billion](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/06/17/business/ai-drugs-development-terray.html). And that’s for those that make it all the way, with the process of development notoriously hit-and-miss.

Among drugs that reach human clinical trials, 90% fail, primarily because of inefficacy or unexpected side effects.

AI technology has the capability to [dramatically increase the speed](https://www.pfizer.com/news/articles/artificial_intelligence_on_a_mission_to_make_clinical_drug_development_faster_and_smarter) of getting drugs into the hands of patients.

One of the main ways in which AI does this is by mining the massive amounts of data created in the development process.

Consider that AI could sort through all of this data in a fraction of the time that it takes human researchers to do the same.

AI could notice a specific molecule that unlocks a new treatment or link data from various studies to come up with better drugs.

Meanwhile, Google is betting on the idea that more sophisticated AI models don’t actually need as much data.

Its AlphaFold3 model, a collaboration between DeepMind and AI drug discovery firm [Isomorphic](https://www.isomorphiclabs.com/), predicts how molecules and proteins will react.

**_![Image 26: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/VdBUKzRSHGUhp7f0IIsO)With so many proteins in existence, manually testing their molecular composition and how they all interact is slow and inefficient.[AlphaFold tries to solve this problem](https://deepmind.google/technologies/alphafold/)._**

When it comes to predicting local structures, AlphaFold3 [reached 97% of its maximum performance](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07487-w) within 20,000 training steps.

AI can also be used to conduct [human-like trials](https://www.politico.eu/article/ai-is-about-to-remake-the-pharmaceutical-drug-medicines-industry/) in the place of animal trials.

That’s the case for a potential ALS drug created by [Verge Genomics](https://www.vergegenomics.com/) through AI.

The company’s AI is able to utilize human data to create human models on the platform and use those to test the drug.

Verge’s drug is [now in the second stage of human trials](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06215755). Phase 1 found the ALS drug to be[safe, well-tolerated and potentially best-in-class](https://www.vergegenomics.com/news-blog/verge-genomics-announces-positive-safety-and-tolerability-data-from-the-phase-1-clinical-trial-of-vrg50635-a-potential-best-in-class-therapeutic-for-all-forms-of-als).

[Exscientia](https://www.exscientia.ai/our-mission), an AI drug discovery company founded in 2012, currently has [two drugs in human trials](https://www.exscientia.ai/pipeline), one aimed at treating cancer and one aimed at treating inflammatory diseases.

**_![Image 27: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/fu1Afv0qSaqzpJ0m18Lo)Search volume for “Exscientia” has jumped 529% in the past 5 years._**

The company [spent $29.8 million on further research and development](https://investors.exscientia.ai/press-releases/press-release-details/2024/Exscientia-Business-Update-for-First-Quarter-2024/default.aspx) in Q1 2024.

And Nvidia and Pfizer [recently invested $80 million](https://aibusiness.com/verticals/nvidia-pfizer-back-ai-drug-discovery-startup) into another AI drug discovery business, [CytoReason](https://www.cytoreason.com/).

### 6. AI Confronts Environmental Questions Head-On

In the future, questions surrounding [AI and its impact on the environment](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2212827124001173) will likely continue to swirl.

On one hand, AI applications could improve sustainability and lead to innovative environmentally-friendly practices.

However, the technology behind AI requires massive amounts of computational resources, which are characteristically damaging to the environment.

**_![Image 28: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/Ul3afilpQyOwv9Mjv6cc)“AI environmental impact” is an area of growing concern._**

**AI computing demands are growing quickly.**

Google’s emissions have [climbed by almost 50% in the last 5 years](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/article/2024/jul/02/google-ai-emissions), and it cited the environmental impact of AI as one of the reasons its net-zero 2030 target “won’t be easy”.

The “AI overviews” it presents in response to search queries [consume 10x more power than a traditional Google search](https://www.levernews.com/the-unknown-toll-of-the-ai-takeover/) - equivalent to talking for roughly an hour on an old-school home phone.

**_![Image 29: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/dpLhJJjaRyCJDz6CiiGY)AI is power-intensive._**

Unfortunately, the negative impact on the environment begins long before the AI system is up and running. The manufacturing of AI solutions is also problematic.

[Manufacturing computer chips](https://fortune.com/2024/01/29/chips-act-semiconductor-factories-environmental-impact-water-electricity-carbon-chemical-waste/) requires huge amounts of energy, uses billions of gallons of fresh water, and discharges hundreds of tons of hazardous waste.

**But AI has helped society make incredible strides toward a more sustainable future, too.**

PwC estimates that using AI for sustainability applications could [reduce global greenhouse gas emissions by as much as 4%](https://www.pwc.co.uk/services/sustainability-climate-change/insights/how-ai-future-can-enable-sustainable-future.html) by 2030.

**_![Image 30: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/vXOcv99yQA2BV2jjXKMy)AI applications have the potential to increase GDP by 4.4% by 2030._**

The technology is utilized for making [calculations and predictions about the environment](https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2024/02/ai-combat-climate-change/#:~:text=The%20use%20of%20artificial%20intelligence,the%20World%20Economic%20Forum%20says.) based on a huge amount of data. AI can see trends and patterns that are nearly impossible for humans to see.

For instance, AI has been trained to measure changes in icebergs 10,000 times more quickly than humans can.

While NASA and IBM have [trained a model specifically designed to help tackle environmental issues](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/ai-open-science-climate-change/), and made it free to access.

On a more day-to-day level, AI technologies can have an impact on sustainability [in a variety of industries](https://blog.google/outreach-initiatives/entrepreneurs/how-4-startups-are-using-ai-to-solve-climate-change-challenges/).

AI can [enable agriculture sensors](https://agro-scout.com/) so farmers use less water, help restaurants [identify and prevent food waste](https://medium.com/@meredithfosterjo/leveraging-ai-to-reduce-food-waste-in-restaurants-451e44d98c9c), and [decrease energy use in factories](https://eugenie.ai/), just to name a few examples.

**The technology is also instrumental in the clean energy sector.**

**_![Image 31: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/P4GDpIFRtSzSh88STsAg)Search interest in “energy transition” is up 305% in the past 5 years._**

In the wind energy sector, AI has a [wide variety of applications](https://www.utmconsultants.com/news/5-areas-ai-will-transform-in-offshore-wind/42396/).

It can help with the scheduling of construction, where highly-specialized teams are often booked up two years ahead of time.

And once wind farms are up and running, AI can enable better monitoring of the turbines. That can [increase their life-span by 10%](https://www.datategy.net/2024/01/17/wind-turbine-optimization-with-ai/).

Meanwhile, as AI helps clean energy, clean energy helps AI, tackling the problem of energy-intensive data centers.

Google’s Hamina data center in Finland is [97% carbon-free](https://blog.google/around-the-globe/google-europe/our-first-offsite-heat-recovery-project-lands-in-finland/), and its heat recapture technology will meet 80% of heat demand in the district.

**_![Image 32: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/d5W2TfBjTSufViYnt0jG)Google’s Hamina data center in Finland runs highly efficiently._**

### 7. Governments Get To Grips With AI Regulation

The regulation of AI is a factor that many will be watching in the coming months and years.

**_![Image 33: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/Qpxl4YqRsy3p6ori3cKI)Search volume for “AI regulation” has climbed 1,440% in 5 years._**

The [2024 Edelman Trust Barometer](https://www.edelman.com/trust/2024/trust-barometer) found that only 30% of Americans trust AI technology. Interestingly, Democrats were significantly more likely to do so (38%) than Republicans (24%).

**And trust in AI companies has actually fallen - from 50% in 2019 to just 35% today.**

Elon Musk and other tech executives asked for a [six-month pause on the development of AI models more advanced than GPT-4](https://www.reuters.com/technology/musk-experts-urge-pause-training-ai-systems-that-can-outperform-gpt-4-2023-03-29/), a plea which fell on deaf ears. But we are seeing a regulatory response.

The EU has passed an “[Artificial Intelligence Act](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2024/05/21/artificial-intelligence-ai-act-council-gives-final-green-light-to-the-first-worldwide-rules-on-ai/)”, which will see the Commission establish an AI Office, and impose checks and regulations on “high-risk” AI systems.

Federal legislation in the US is yet to arrive. But an [executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2023/10/30/fact-sheet-president-biden-issues-executive-order-on-safe-secure-and-trustworthy-artificial-intelligence/) has been passed that requires “the most powerful AI systems” to share safety test results with the government, among other things.

At the state level, Colorado became the first state to pass comprehensive AI legislation. In May 2024, it [passed the Colorado AI Act](https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/newly-passed-colorado-ai-act-will-impose-obligations-developers-and-deployers-high#:~:text=The%20Colorado%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act,consequential%20decisions%20by%20such%20systems.).

Effective from February 2026, it mirrors the EU in defining “high-risk” AI systems - ones that “when deployed, make, or are a substantial factor in making a consequential decision”.

The legislation imposes duties on those systems to take care to avoid bias and discrimination.

**It’s clear that the drive for responsible AI is underway.**

**_![Image 34: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/8khMNIFPQpWKUt5PEIq9)Search volume for “responsible AI” is up 3233% since 2019._**

The key tenets of [responsible AI](https://www.accenture.com/us-en/services/applied-intelligence/ai-ethics-governance) center on developing and deploying the technology in a fair and trustworthy way.

It also means that organizations ensure transparency, minimize bias, protect data, and provide a way for individuals to raise concerns.

**_![Image 35: undefined](https://cdn.buttercms.com/output=f:webp/2PEBKJrySfiwEVUY20QS)Organizations deploying responsible AI are watching for potential bias and promoting transparency._**

Still, some in the industry say government regulation isn’t needed to achieve this. Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI [all made voluntary self-regulation commitments](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/07/22/1095193/ai-companies-promised-the-white-house-to-self-regulate-one-year-ago-whats-changed)to the White House last year.

And critics warn that government regulations could slow progress and set the United States up to [fall behind China](https://www.foxnews.com/media/regulation-allow-china-dominate-artificial-intelligence-race-experts-warn-we-will-lose) in terms of dominating the future global technology.

### Conclusion

As AI continues to advance, it will not only change the way companies operate but also the way individuals live. From personalized healthcare to [automated investing](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/ai-investing), AI has the potential to revolutionize nearly every aspect of business.

Of course, there are many challenges associated with the future of AI technology. But there are countless opportunities available for bold innovators, and a proliferation of [AI courses and certifications](https://explodingtopics.com/blog/best-ai-courses) are helping people get to grips with it.

The future of AI is certain to be a rapidly evolving landscape.
